summary: Del Norte County lookout site. The CCC's 1934 Camp Six lookout was moved to Bear Basin Butte; only unexplained remains are reported at the original site.

facts.status_note: Original site: only remains are reported (2019 photo). The Camp Six lookout was moved to Bear Basin Butte.

events.note: A September 1916 Siskiyou Bulletin item, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, says a lookout tower on U.P. Coon Mtn. had been abandoned. Unclear whether it is the same structure as the 1934 lookout.
Constructed by the CCC as the Camp Six Lookout on Upper Coon Mountain. A peakbagging note says a structure stood on the site before 1935.

The Register says that in the 1950s the site was compromised with a number of electronic facilities and the lookout was decommissioned. 1950 is a placeholder for that decade; the source gives no single year.
Restoration of the Camp Six began in 1991. Vandals later damaged it further, and the Forest Service removed, rebuilt and relocated it to Bear Basin Butte.

corrections.why: peakbagging.com places the original site in Six Rivers National Forest. The Forest Lookouts page places it in Siskiyou National Forest. The Register lists Six Rivers for the relocated Camp Six at Bear Basin Butte, not for the original site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1916 notice describes an abandoned lookout tower on U.P. Coon Mtn.; the Register credits a CCC lookout built on Upper Coon Mountain in 1934. The sources do not say whether they are the same structure, so the record uses 1934 for the Camp Six build and the story says the question is open.
The Forest Lookouts page says Siskiyou National Forest; peakbagging.com says Six Rivers National Forest. The record uses Six Rivers, the placement for the original site, and the story reports both.

sources.title: Camp Six Lookout at Bear Basin Butte

notes_for_editor: Bear Basin Butte record should carry the Camp Six relocation: NHLR lists it as US 288, CA 21, registered January 6, 1999, nominated by the Gasquet Ranger District, and available for rental. Peakbagging.com says it moved its own pin after Dean Gaudet located the site; check the FFLA coordinates 41.81861, -123.86333 against that. The 1916 tower and the 1934 CCC lookout may be different structures. The 1950 event year is a placeholder for 'the 1950s'. No access or visit information for the original site was found.
